affected_system: fixed-route public transit service and passenger connections
alternatives: verify the highest-consequence signals before acting on route-segment delay propagation and transfer failure
combine targeted inspection, monitoring, and data-quality repair for route-segment delay propagation and transfer failure
pair vehicle-trajectory and timetable dependency diagnosis with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Trips, stops, vehicle observations, disruptions, and calendars share a versioned service day.
Passenger loads and transfer behavior are measured or represented as bounded assumptions.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: continue current inspection and reporting practice for route-segment delay propagation and transfer failure.

constraints.description: The transit reliability and passenger continuity diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: transit chief operating officer and service-planning director
decision_question: Which route segments and transfer nodes repeatedly propagate delay into passenger connection failures?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The transit reliability and passenger continuity diagnose must respect declared measurement resolution and classification uncertainty.
independence_key.decision_object: route-segment delay propagation and transfer failure
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for route-segment delay propagation and transfer failure passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.

intended_claim: A versioned diagnose design for comparing declared alternatives affecting route-segment delay propagation and transfer failure, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: distributional gap in passenger-weighted missed connections
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not infer passenger experience from vehicle delay without validated load and transfer evidence.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for route-segment delay propagation and transfer failure passes documented checks for coverage, semantics, geography, timestamps, and uncertainty.

title: Diagnose transit delay propagation and missed connections
transportability_risks: Fare policy, headways, fleet, labor rules, topology, and passenger behavior vary by operator.
Reliability metrics may not transfer between schedule-based and frequency-based service.
